title: Conjecture 1.5
statement_text: The unique maximal Schnyder wood of the UIHPT is the weak limit of the maximal Schnyder wood of a uniformly random triangulation from $T^m_n$ as $n \to \infty$ and then $m \to \infty$.
context_text: $T^m_n$ is the set of simple $2$-connected triangulations of an $(m+2)$-gon with $n$ interior vertices, rooted at a boundary edge. The UIPT with boundary length $m$ is the local (weak, for balls around the root) limit as $n\to\infty$ of a uniform element of $T^m_n$, and the UIHPT (uniform infinite half-planar triangulation) is the local limit of the UIPT of the $(m+2)$-gon as $m\to\infty$. A Schnyder wood of a triangulation rooted at a boundary edge $(v_r,v_y)$ is an orientation of the edges together with a colouring in red, yellow and blue such that: every interior vertex has exactly three outgoing edges, coloured blue, red, yellow in anticlockwise order, and every incoming edge enters between the outgoing edges of the two other colours; $v_y$ has no outgoing edge and only incoming yellow edges, $v_r$ has one outgoing edge and only incoming red edges; every other boundary vertex has exactly two outgoing edges, red and yellow, and, anticlockwise from the boundary, its incident edges are incoming yellow, outgoing red, incoming blue, outgoing yellow, incoming red. A Schnyder wood is maximal if it has no anticlockwise directed cycle and, for infinite triangulations, no right-directed two-ended infinite path (one leaving the boundary on its right, an 'infinite anticlockwise cycle'). Every finite triangulation has a unique maximal Schnyder wood. The authors prove that every infinite triangulation with finite boundary has a unique maximal Schnyder wood, that the maximal Schnyder wood of the UIPT with boundary length $m$ is the weak limit of the maximal Schnyder wood of a uniform element of $T^m_n$ as $n\to\infty$, and that the UIHPT almost surely has a unique maximal Schnyder wood, which they construct by repeated peeling processes and whose monochromatic subgraphs they describe. The natural peeling process started from a fixed root edge almost surely never explores most of the UIHPT, and this non-locality prevented them from proving the corresponding convergence when $m\to\infty$ after $n\to\infty$. They discuss potential consequences for geodesic paths and for the winding of monochromatic trees in large finite triangulations.

title: Open question on Schnyder woods for general half-plane triangulations
statement_text: It would be interesting to know whether Schnyder woods exist on all half-plane triangulations, and if not, to characterise the ones for which they do exist.
context_text: $T^m_n$ is the set of simple $2$-connected triangulations of an $(m+2)$-gon with $n$ interior vertices, rooted at a boundary edge. The UIPT with boundary length $m$ is the local (weak, for balls around the root) limit as $n\to\infty$ of a uniform element of $T^m_n$, and the UIHPT (uniform infinite half-planar triangulation) is the local limit of the UIPT of the $(m+2)$-gon as $m\to\infty$. A Schnyder wood of a triangulation rooted at a boundary edge $(v_r,v_y)$ is an orientation of the edges together with a colouring in red, yellow and blue such that: every interior vertex has exactly three outgoing edges, coloured blue, red, yellow in anticlockwise order, and every incoming edge enters between the outgoing edges of the two other colours; $v_y$ has no outgoing edge and only incoming yellow edges, $v_r$ has one outgoing edge and only incoming red edges; every other boundary vertex has exactly two outgoing edges, red and yellow, and, anticlockwise from the boundary, its incident edges are incoming yellow, outgoing red, incoming blue, outgoing yellow, incoming red. Every finite triangulation has a unique maximal Schnyder wood. A half-plane triangulation is an infinite (one-ended) triangulation with infinite boundary. The authors prove existence and uniqueness of the maximal Schnyder wood for every infinite triangulation with finite boundary and almost surely for the UIHPT; their construction also gives Schnyder woods on other half-plane triangulations with similar properties, and whenever a maximal Schnyder wood of a half-plane triangulation exists it is unique. Existence in general is left open.

title: Open question on local limit of uniformly random wooded triangulations
statement_text: It would be interesting to understand the local limit of uniformly random wooded triangulations as the boundary length tends to infinity, and whether such wooded triangulations have a local limit, which would be a random wooded triangulation of the half-plane different from the one constructed in this work.
context_text: $T^m_n$ is the set of simple $2$-connected triangulations of an $(m+2)$-gon with $n$ interior vertices, rooted at a boundary edge. The UIPT with boundary length $m$ is the local (weak, for balls around the root) limit as $n\to\infty$ of a uniform element of $T^m_n$, and the UIHPT (uniform infinite half-planar triangulation) is the local limit of the UIPT of the $(m+2)$-gon as $m\to\infty$. A Schnyder wood of a triangulation rooted at a boundary edge $(v_r,v_y)$ is an orientation of the edges together with a colouring in red, yellow and blue such that: every interior vertex has exactly three outgoing edges, coloured blue, red, yellow in anticlockwise order, and every incoming edge enters between the outgoing edges of the two other colours; $v_y$ has no outgoing edge and only incoming yellow edges, $v_r$ has one outgoing edge and only incoming red edges; every other boundary vertex has exactly two outgoing edges, red and yellow, and, anticlockwise from the boundary, its incident edges are incoming yellow, outgoing red, incoming blue, outgoing yellow, incoming red. A Schnyder wood is maximal if it has no anticlockwise directed cycle and, for infinite triangulations, no right-directed two-ended infinite path (one leaving the boundary on its right, an 'infinite anticlockwise cycle'). Every finite triangulation has a unique maximal Schnyder wood. A wooded triangulation is a triangulation together with a Schnyder wood; a uniformly random wooded triangulation is uniform over such pairs, which differs from taking the maximal Schnyder wood of a uniform triangulation. By results of Bernardi and Bonichon, the heights of the trees in a uniform wooded triangulation with $n$ faces are $\Theta(\sqrt n)$ in probability and in expectation, while in the maximal Schnyder wood of a uniform triangulation the height of a uniformly random vertex has expectation of order $n^{3/4}$ (Chapuy). The authors construct the maximal Schnyder wood of the UIHPT; a local limit of uniformly random wooded triangulations as the boundary length tends to infinity, if it exists, would be a different random wooded triangulation of the half-plane.
